topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Besides source of funds, which of the following is also a Virginia-specific protected class not among the federal Fair Housing Act's seven protected classes?
choice_a: Sexual orientation
choice_b: Religion
choice_c: Sex
choice_d: National origin
explanation: Virginia's Fair Housing Law adds sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, elderliness, and source of funds as protected classes beyond the federal Fair Housing Act's seven (race, color, religion, national origin, sex, familial status, disability).

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Which Virginia-added protected class prohibits housing discrimination based on a person's internal sense of gender, which may differ from the sex assigned at birth?
choice_a: Gender identity
choice_b: Familial status
choice_c: Disability
choice_d: Color
explanation: Gender identity is one of the Virginia-specific classes added to the state's fair housing protections beyond the federal Fair Housing Act's seven classes.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Which Virginia-added protected class is intended to prevent housing discrimination against current or former service members?
choice_a: Military status
choice_b: Race
choice_c: National origin
choice_d: Religion
explanation: Military status is a Virginia-specific protected class not found in the federal Fair Housing Act's list of seven classes.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, 'familial status' includes which of the following?
choice_a: One or more individuals who have not attained the age of 18 being domiciled with a parent or guardian, as well as any pregnant person or a person in the process of securing legal custody of a minor
choice_b: Only married couples with biological children
choice_c: Only households with more than four occupants
choice_d: Any household regardless of the age of its occupants
explanation: Familial status covers minors domiciled with a parent or guardian, and extends to pregnant persons and persons in the process of securing legal custody of a minor.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, 'disability' is defined to include which of the following?
choice_a: (i) a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities; (ii) a record of having such an impairment; or (iii) being regarded as having such an impairment
choice_b: Only a physical impairment that is permanent and visible
choice_c: Only impairments certified by a state agency
choice_d: Only conditions listed on a Social Security disability determination
explanation: The statutory definition of disability is a three-prong test covering an actual substantially limiting impairment, a record of such an impairment, or being regarded as having one.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, does the definition of 'disability' include current illegal use of a controlled substance?
choice_a: No, current illegal use of a controlled substance is excluded from the definition of disability
choice_b: Yes, without any exceptions
choice_c: Only if a doctor prescribed it originally
choice_d: Yes, but only for a first offense
explanation: Current illegal use of a controlled substance is specifically excluded from the statutory definition of disability.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, 'source of funds' is defined as what?
choice_a: Any source that lawfully provides funds to or on behalf of a renter or buyer of housing, including assistance, benefit, or subsidy programs administered by a governmental or nongovernmental entity
choice_b: Only wages paid by a W-2 employer
choice_c: Only funds from a federal housing choice voucher
choice_d: Only cash held in a bank account for at least 90 days
explanation: Source of funds is broadly defined to cover any lawful source of funds provided to or on behalf of a renter or buyer, including government and nongovernment assistance programs.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: As of what date did 'source of funds' become a protected class under the Virginia Fair Housing Law?
choice_a: July 1, 2020
choice_b: January 1, 1991
choice_c: July 1, 1972
choice_d: January 1, 2010
explanation: Source of funds (source of income) was added as a protected class effective July 1, 2020, to address discrimination against renters and buyers who lawfully receive assistance, subsidy, or benefit funds.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.1:1, the term 'discriminatory housing practice' is defined as an act that is unlawful under which sections?
choice_c: Only Title 54.1 Chapter 21
choice_d: Only federal law, since Virginia has no independent definition
explanation: 'Discriminatory housing practice' is defined by cross-reference to the acts made unlawful under 36-96.3 (unlawful practices), 36-96.4 (real estate-related transactions), 36-96.5 (interference), and 36-96.6 (restrictive covenants).

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(A), even an owner who qualifies for the private-individual single-family-house exemption remains bound by which requirements?
choice_a: The nondiscriminatory-advertising requirement of 36-96.3(A)(3) and the restrictive-covenant provisions of 36-96.6(A) through (C)
choice_b: None -- the exemption removes all fair housing obligations
choice_c: Only the escrow account recordkeeping rules
choice_d: Only the continuing education requirements
explanation: The exemption's opening clause expressly carves out and preserves the discriminatory-advertising prohibition and the restrictive-covenant provisions, so even an exempt private owner is still bound by those.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(C), a religious organization may limit occupancy of dwellings it owns and operates for a noncommercial purpose to persons of the same religion, EXCEPT when what is true?
choice_a: Membership in the religion is itself restricted on account of race, color, national origin, sex, elderliness, familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military status, or disability
choice_b: The dwelling has more than four units
choice_c: The organization charges any rent at all
choice_d: The dwelling is located outside of Virginia
explanation: The religious-organization exemption does not apply if membership in the religion itself discriminates based on one of the chapter's protected classes.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(D), may a housing provider deny housing to an individual based on a conviction for what?
choice_a: Illegal manufacture or distribution of a controlled substance
choice_b: Any misdemeanor traffic violation
choice_c: Any arrest, regardless of conviction
choice_d: Failure to pay a parking ticket
explanation: The Fair Housing Law does not prohibit denying housing based on a conviction for the illegal manufacture or distribution of a controlled substance.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(E), an owner may deny rental to an applicant who poses what?
choice_a: A clear and present threat of substantial harm to others or to the dwelling itself
choice_b: A minor personality conflict with the owner
choice_c: A low credit score alone
choice_d: A different political affiliation than the owner
explanation: The law does not prohibit denying rental to an applicant who poses a clear and present threat of substantial harm to other residents or to the dwelling.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(H), may a landlord consider an applicant's status as a victim of family abuse?
choice_a: Yes, a landlord may consider evidence of an applicant's status as a family abuse victim to mitigate an adverse effect on an otherwise qualified applicant's application
choice_b: No, family abuse history may never be discussed
choice_c: Only if the applicant is applying jointly with the abuser
choice_d: Only for public housing applicants
explanation: The chapter allows a landlord to consider family-abuse-victim status specifically to mitigate an adverse effect on an otherwise qualified applicant's rental application.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(I), the source-of-funds protection does not apply to an owner who denies or limits rental based on source of funds, provided the owner does not own more than how many rental dwelling units in Virginia?
choice_a: Four
choice_b: Ten
choice_c: Two
choice_d: Twenty
explanation: A small-landlord exemption from the source-of-funds protection applies where the owner does not own more than four rental dwelling units in the Commonwealth at the time of the alleged discriminatory practice.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(I), the small-landlord source-of-funds exemption is unavailable if the owner, individually or through a business entity, owns what?
choice_a: More than a 10 percent interest in more than four rental dwelling units in the Commonwealth
choice_b: Any interest whatsoever in a second property
choice_c: A property management company
choice_d: A single rental unit valued over $500,000
explanation: The exemption does not apply if the owner, whether individually or through a business entity, owns more than a 10 percent interest in more than four rental dwelling units in Virginia.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.2(J), is it unlawful for an owner to deny or limit rental based on source of funds if that funding source is not approved within how many days of the tenancy-approval request submission?
choice_a: 15 days
choice_b: 60 days
choice_c: 5 days
choice_d: 45 days
explanation: It is not unlawful to deny or limit rental based on source of funds if that funding source is not approved within 15 days of the person submitting the request for tenancy approval.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(A)(1), what constitutes an unlawful discriminatory housing practice?
choice_a: Refusing to sell or rent after the making of a bona fide offer, or otherwise making a dwelling unavailable, because of a protected class
choice_b: Declining to accept a lowball offer below list price
choice_c: Requiring proof of income for all applicants equally
choice_d: Requesting a security deposit consistent with local law
explanation: Refusing to sell or rent after a bona fide offer, or otherwise making a dwelling unavailable, because of a protected class is a core unlawful practice.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(A)(2), it is unlawful to do what because of a protected class?
choice_a: Discriminate in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling, or in the provision of services or facilities in connection with it
choice_b: Offer identical lease terms to every applicant
choice_c: Charge the same application fee to every applicant
choice_d: Apply the same credit-score cutoff to every applicant
explanation: Discriminating in the terms, conditions, or privileges of a sale or rental, or in related services and facilities, because of a protected class is unlawful.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(A)(5), it is unlawful to deny a person access to what because of a protected class?
choice_a: Membership or participation in a multiple listing service, real estate brokers' organization, or other facility relating to the business of selling or renting dwellings
choice_b: A parking space at the brokerage's office
choice_c: A copy of the licensee's personal calendar
choice_d: The firm's internal payroll system
explanation: Denying access to an MLS, real estate brokers' organization, or related facility, or discriminating in the terms of that access, because of a protected class is unlawful.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(A)(7), 'blockbusting' -- inducing an owner to sell or rent by representations regarding the entry of persons of a particular protected class into the neighborhood -- is what?
choice_a: An unlawful discriminatory housing practice
choice_b: A permissible marketing technique if factually accurate
choice_c: Only unlawful if done in writing
choice_d: Only unlawful if the licensee profits directly from the resulting sale
explanation: Inducing or attempting to induce a sale or rental by representations about the entry of a protected class into a neighborhood is an unlawful discriminatory housing practice, regardless of accuracy or medium.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(B), for multifamily dwellings designed and constructed after March 13, 1991, discrimination includes failing to ensure what?
choice_a: Accessible common areas, doorways wide enough for wheelchairs, accessible routes, usable environmental controls, reinforced bathroom walls for grab bars, and usable kitchens and bathrooms for wheelchair users
choice_b: A minimum of one parking space per unit
choice_c: Central air conditioning in every unit
choice_d: A swimming pool on the premises
explanation: Post-March 13, 1991 multifamily construction must meet specific accessible-design requirements; failing to meet them is treated as discrimination under this section.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3(B), when a landlord conditions permission for a disability-related modification on the tenant restoring the interior afterward, must the tenant restore damage from reasonable wear and tear?

choice_c: The landlord may never require any restoration
choice_d: Restoration may only be required if the tenant is a first-time renter
explanation: A landlord may reasonably condition permission for a modification on the tenant restoring the interior to its original condition, but reasonable wear and tear is excepted from that restoration duty.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3:1, when a person's disability and disability-related need for an assistance animal are both obvious or otherwise known, may a housing provider demand documentation?
choice_a: No, no additional verification may be demanded when the disability or need is already obvious or otherwise known
choice_b: Yes, documentation is always required regardless of obviousness
choice_c: Only a veterinary certificate may be required
choice_d: Only if the animal is not a dog
explanation: If the disability or the disability-related need is obvious or already known to the housing provider, no additional verification may be demanded.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3:1, when documentation of a disability-related need for an assistance animal may properly be requested, which of the following is an acceptable source of that documentation?
choice_a: A member of a reliable, non-fee-based peer support group who has actual knowledge of the disability
choice_b: Only a board-certified psychiatrist
choice_c: Only a document notarized by the housing provider
choice_d: Only the local animal control office
explanation: Acceptable documentation sources include mental health service providers, licensed professionals, non-fee-based peer support group members, and caregivers or government entities with actual knowledge of the disability.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3:1, a person who knowingly provides fraudulent documentation to support a request for an assistance animal accommodation is subject to what?

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.3:2, if granting a requested accommodation might impose a significant burden, what must the housing provider do?

explanation: Section 36-96.5 makes it unlawful to coerce, intimidate, threaten, or interfere with a person for exercising fair housing rights or for aiding or encouraging another person's exercise of those rights.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.6, if a deed or other instrument conveying property contains a void discriminatory restrictive covenant, may the grantee refuse to accept the document until the covenant is removed?

choice_b: As commercial establishments

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts

question: Under VA Code 36-96.7, does housing for older persons lose its exempt status merely because some existing residents who moved in before September 13, 1988 do not meet the age requirements?

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.9, within how many days after a complaint is filed must the Board give the respondent written notice of the alleged discriminatory housing practice?

question: Under VA Code 36-96.11, the Board's determination of whether reasonable cause exists that a discriminatory housing practice occurred must be made after consultation with whom?
choice_a: The Office of the Attorney General
choice_b: The local sheriff's office
choice_c: The National Association of Realtors

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.13, are conciliation agreements resolving a fair housing complaint automatically kept confidential?

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts

choice_a: Not later than two years

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under VA Code 36-96.18, can a court's relief in a private fair housing civil action disturb a property sale already consummated before the relief was granted, involving a good-faith purchaser without notice?
choice_a: No, such relief may not affect a sale, encumbrance, or lease consummated before the granting of relief and involving a bona fide purchaser without actual notice of the complaint or civil action
choice_b: Yes, all such sales are automatically voided

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, is having a professional or occupational license suspended, revoked, or surrendered in connection with disciplinary action IN ANY JURISDICTION itself listed as a prohibited act?

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, is knowingly providing false, misleading, or incomplete information in response to an inquiry by the Board or its agents a prohibited act?

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, is a principal or supervising broker's failure to ensure proper supervision and accountability over the firm's escrow account and daily financial dealings a prohibited act?
choice_a: Yes, this failure is expressly listed as a prohibited act

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-260, is a broker's failure to disburse escrow funds according to Board regulations, or failure to retain documents supporting the basis for disbursal, a prohibited act?
choice_a: Yes, both failing to properly disburse escrow funds and failing to retain the supporting disbursal documentation are listed as prohibited acts

choice_c: Only disbursal errors count; recordkeeping failures do not
choice_d: Only if the escrow account earns interest
explanation: A broker's failure to disburse escrow funds according to regulation, or failure to properly retain documents relating to the basis for disbursal, is a listed prohibited act.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-280, is offering to pay or paying valuable consideration to a person not licensed in any jurisdiction for services that require a real estate license a prohibited act?
choice_a: Yes, this is expressly prohibited

choice_d: Only if the payment exceeds $1,000

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-280, is it a prohibited act to gain a financial benefit from property or transaction information obtained through licensed activity, without proper written approval?
choice_a: Yes, this improper financial dealing is prohibited

explanation: Gaining a financial benefit from property or transaction information obtained through licensed work, without the proper written approvals, is a prohibited improper financial dealing.

topic: Virginia Fair Housing Law & Prohibited Acts
question: Under 18VAC135-20-300, a standard agent representing a seller or landlord must timely disclose to a prospective buyer or tenant what, if actually known to the licensee?
choice_a: All material adverse facts pertaining to the physical condition of the property
